title: Research method: Tissue-specific gene expression in mouse founder strains
bodyHtml:
Study #1: The influence of strain and sex on gene regulation in multiple metabolic tissues.

This study sequenced the transcriptome in five tissues (pancreatic islets, liver, white adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and heart) collected from male and female mice of the eight founder strains of the Diversity Outbred (DO) mouse stock. The founder strains are A/J, C57BL/6J (B6), 129S1/SvImJ (129), NOD/ShiLtJ (NOD), NZO/HILtJ (NZO), CAST/EiJ (CAST), PWK/PhJ (PWK) and WSB/EiJ (WSB), were obtained from the Jackson Labs, and maintained at the University of Wisconsin-Madison animal vivarium within the Biochemistry Department.

To induce a metabolic challenge, all mice were maintained on a Western-style diet that was high in fat (45% kcal) and carbohydrate (41% kcal). At ~5 weeks of age, the mice were maintained on the Western-style diet for ~16 weeks prior to sacrifice for tissue collection, except NZO males, which were sacrificed after 9 weeks. Approximately 60 mice were used for gene expression profiling in extra-islet tissues; 95 mice were used to sequence the islet transcriptome.

For each tissue, raw read counts from the RNA-sequencing were quantified by EMASE and normalized by DESeq2 to yield variance stabilizing transformation (VST) of expression values for all genes. An ANOVA was performed to identify genes that showed differential expression by strain, sex, or strain-by-sex interaction. To control for false discovery rate, P-values were adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. This analysis identified ~19,000 genes that were differentially regulated as a function of strain (Adjusted P-value < 1e-5) in one or more of the five tissues profiled. Many of the genes that demonstrate strain-dependent regulation have human homologues that are strongly associated with one or more phenotypes in human GWAS.

Study #2: The influence of strain, sex, and diet on hepatic gene regulation.

This study sequenced the transcriptome in liver tissue collected from male and female mice of the eight founder strains of the Diversity Outbred (DO) mouse stock described in Study #1. Mice were obtained from the Jackson Labs and maintained at the University of Wisconsin-Madison animal vivarium within the Biochemistry Department. A total of 192 mice were included in this study.

Mice were divided into two dietary groups. The first group was fed a diet high in fat (45% kcal), while the second group was fed a diet high in carbohydrates (41% kcal). At ~5 weeks of age, the mice were maintained on the diet for ~16 weeks prior to sacrifice for tissue collection, except NZO males, which were sacrificed after 9 weeks.

Sequence alignment was performed on raw RNA Seq reads using STAR aligner software. Transcript-level quantification was then performed on aligned reads using RSEM software to obtain gene- and isoform-level abundance estimates. Raw (TPM) counts estimates were then imported into R/DESeq2 to produce variance stabilizing transformed (VST) expression values for genes and isoforms.

An ANOVA was performed to identify genes that showed differential expression by strain, sex, diet, or the interactions between these variables, using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to control the false discovery rate. As in Study #1, strain exerted the strongest influence, where ~13,500 genes were differentially regulated in response to strain differences among the mice (Adjusted P-value < 1e-5). Sex, strain-by-sex and strain-by-diet interactions all yielded significant differences in >1,000 genes (Adjusted P-value < 0.05).
